newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin resumes vacation after Moscow talks.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin resumes vacation after Moscow talks.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin left Moscow for the Black Sea resort of Sochi on Thursday to resume a holiday he interrupted to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin.

The presidential press service said Yeltsin had flown to Sochi after talks with Jiang and a ceremony at which they signed a treaty with the presidents of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan intended to reduce border troops.
Interfax news agency said Yeltsin, 66, would probably return to Moscow on May 4. He is expected to host Spain's King Juan Carlos in the first half of May.

Yeltsin still hopes to travel to Paris for the anticipated signing on May 27 of a landmark security accord between Moscow and NATO, Interfax quoted presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.

Russia has recently sounded an optimistic note about the chances of clinching the agreement, despite its continued strong opposition to the Western alliance's plans to take in former communist countries in eastern and central Europe.
